blocks.html:
Declares a search index. Like `defineLink`, the file registers itself on
import: the application loads every file under `search/` and hands what was
registered to the Search Module as its `indexes` option, so the module has one
input rather than a registry and an option that can disagree.

`fields` must be a schema from `search.define({ ... })`. The documents
`seed` yields are type-checked against the declared fields.

children.name: name
children.description:
The index's unique name, which is what `query.search({ entity })` resolves
against.

children.name: entity
children.description: The `query.graph` entrypoint used to hydrate non-indexed fields.

children.name: primary_key
children.description:
The field whose value keys the index's documents, which is what a hit's `id`
holds.

children.name: provider
children.description:
The identifier of the provider backing this index. Defaults to the module's
configured default provider.

children.name: settings
children.description: The settings applied to the index when it's created or migrated.

children.name: typo_tolerance
children.description: How misspelled terms are matched.

children.name: distinct_attribute
children.description:
The dotted path of a field that hits are deduplicated by, returning at most
one hit per distinct value. Overridden per query by `search_options.distinct`.

children.name: provider_options
children.description: Index settings specific to a search engine, keyed by provider identifier.

children.name: events
children.description: Events related and that can affect the data for this index.

children.name: type
children.description: The field's type.

children.name: array
children.description: Whether the field holds an array of the declared `type`.

children.name: searchable
children.description:
Whether the field is matched against a free-text query, optionally with a
`weight` boosting its relevance. The weight is applied at build time on some
engines, such as Meilisearch and Algolia, and at query time on others, such
as Typesense and Elasticsearch.

children.name: filterable
children.description: Whether the field can be used in a query's filters.

children.name: sortable
children.description: Whether results can be sorted by the field.

children.name: facetable
children.description:
Whether the field can be faceted, and which facet types it supports.
Defaults to `["value"]`, or `["range"]` for numeric and date fields.
`"stats"` is opt-in, since implying it would make numeric fields unusable on
providers without aggregations.

children.name: retrievable
children.description:
Whether the field comes back on hits. `false` for index-only fields, such as a
blob used purely for matching. `query.search` reads this to decide which
requested fields the engine can serve and which need `query.graph`.

Vector fields default to not retrievable — embeddings are not useful on
hits. Set `retrievable: true`, or `.retrievable()` in the DSL, to return
them.

children.name: dimensions
children.description:
The dimensionality of the embedding stored in a `type: "vector"` field.
Required for vector fields; meaningless on any other type. When `embed` is
omitted, every vector written to the field must have exactly this many
components.

children.name: embed
children.description:
When `true` on a vector field, documents pass a string and the engine
embeds it at write time, and for `search_options.vector.query` at query
time. Omit `embed` to supply embeddings yourself as a `number[]`.

children.name: enabled
children.description: Whether typo tolerance is enabled at all.

children.name: min_word_size_for_one_typo
children.description:
The shortest term length that tolerates a single typo. A provider with a
higher floor of its own rejects a shorter length from `upsertIndex`; one
that doesn't match by edit distance at all ignores this.

children.name: min_word_size_for_two_typos
children.description:
The shortest term length that tolerates two typos. Cannot be lower than
`min_word_size_for_one_typo`. Ignored by a provider that doesn't match by
edit distance.

children.name: disabled_on_attributes
children.description:
The dotted paths of the fields that must always match exactly, such as a
SKU or a handle. A provider that can't exclude a single field rejects
this rather than fuzzy-matching it anyway.

one hit per distinct value. Overridden per query by `search_options.distinct`.

types.name: consume
types.description: Executed on event ingestion to determine the action that needs to be performed on the index.

types.name: seed
types.description:
Yields mutations in batches — the same shape `consume` returns, so a
seed can express a delete, not just an upsert. Ran when there is no data
in the index, on reindex, and for the catch-up pass after a full seed.

blocks.html:
Builds an index definition's `consume` from a `query.graph` query.

The event's IDs are read back through `query.graph` and upserted. An ID the
read doesn't return, or whose row the `transform` rejects, is deleted
instead — which is what keeps a row that was removed, unpublished, or
filtered out of the index from lingering in it.

```ts
export default defineSearchIndex({
  name: "product",
  entity: "product",
  fields: productFields,
  events: ["product.created", "product.updated", "product.deleted"],
  consume: graphConsume({ fields: ["id", "title"] }),
  seed: graphSeed({ fields: ["id", "title"] }),
})
```

types.name: TRow
types.description:
`seed`

 and 

`consume`

 implementations backed by 

`query.graph`

.

Nearly every index is a projection of an entity that already lives behind


`query.graph`

, so the helpers simplify catchup, soft-deletes and similar,
which should be enough for most use cases.

children.name: entity
children.description:
The `query.graph` entrypoint to read from. Defaults to the index
definition's `entity`.

children.name: fields
children.description:
The fields to select from `query.graph`. Without a `transform` the row is
indexed as-is, so this should then select exactly what the index declares.

children.name: transform
children.description:
Maps a row to the document to index. Returning `null` or `undefined`
excludes the row, and is how an index that only holds part of an entity
says so — narrowing the read with a filter instead would hide a row that
stops qualifying, leaving its document behind.

`consume` and the catch-up pass turn a rejection into a delete, so an
excluded row leaves the index rather than going stale in it.

Defaults to indexing the row as-is.

children.name: resolve_ids
children.description:
The IDs of the documents the event affects, which are read back through
`query.graph` and written to the index.

Defaults to `event.data.id`, as a single ID or an array of them.

children.name: is_delete
children.description:
Whether the event removes its documents from the index rather than
updating them. A deleted row can't be read back, so it's deleted by ID
without going to `query.graph`.

types.name: (event: Event<any>, context: SearchIngestionContext) => Promise<SearchIndexSeedMutation<Fields>[]>
types.description:
Builds an index definition's `consume` from a `query.graph` query.

The event's IDs are read back through `query.graph` and upserted. An ID the

blocks.html:
Builds an index definition's `seed` from a `query.graph` query.

The seed pages the entity in ascending order of the index' primary key, so
the next page starts after the last row and a run interrupted halfway
resumes from the context's `last_key` rather than restarting. The catch-up
pass that follows a full seed reads the rows touched since it started with
soft-deleted ones included, and turns those — along with any row the
`transform` rejects — into deletes.
